h1: Nap Krabi Hotel, Krabi — a hotel near Krabi Airport with a pool and gym
intro: If you land in Krabi late at night, or you have an early flight that gets you moving before sunrise and you would rather not risk a long drive in the small hours — Nap Krabi Hotel is a name travelers bring up often as Krabi's go-to "stay-before-your-flight" hotel · It's a 4-star property on Phetkasem Road in Krabi Noi sub-district, sitting just about a 5–10 min drive from Krabi Airport (KBV) · What sets it apart from the usual near-airport options is that it has an outdoor pool with a kids' pool, a gym, and a balcony in every room · Open since 2017, certified SHA Extra Plus, with 80 rooms, free parking, breakfast, and a 24-hour front desk · It scores around 7.8 from real reviews on Booking.com and TripAdvisor · From about THB 600/night

body.html: Who Nap Krabi Hotel is for, in a nutshell — to put it as simply as possible, Nap Krabi Hotel is a hotel for people looking for "a place near Krabi Airport that still has a pool and a gym" — a combination you don't run into often, because most places around the airport are guesthouses or small hotels without these amenities · It's not a luxury beachfront resort, and it isn't right on Ao Nang or Railay, but a mid-size 80-room hotel that positions itself as a "base for the start and end of your trip" rather than a destination for the holiday itself · It has been open since 2017 and holds the SHA Extra Plus health-and-safety standard · Real reviews on Booking.com (scoring around 7.1–7.8 from a few hundred guests), TripAdvisor (around 3.7 out of 5, ranked roughly #41 of 94 hotels in Mueang Krabi) and other platforms all point the same way: the people this suits are travelers with late-night or early-morning flights, anyone stopping for a night before or after a flight, small families who want a kids' pool, and self-drivers who want free parking · On the flip side, if you're coming to Krabi to relax by the sea, wake up to a bay view, or walk straight down to the beach from your room, this isn't the answer — look at a resort over on the Ao Nang side or on the islands instead · But in its role as a clean near-airport hotel with a pool and gym at an accessible price, Nap Krabi does its job well enough, and an overall score in the high 7s confirms that people who arrive with expectations matched to what the hotel actually is come away reasonably happy

Location and getting around — this is both the selling point and the thing you most need to understand clearly about Nap Krabi Hotel · The hotel sits on Phetkasem Road in Krabi Noi sub-district, Mueang Krabi district, an area between Krabi town and the airport · Its number-one strength is being just about 3–6 km, or roughly a 5–10 min drive, from Krabi Airport (KBV), which makes it a popular pick for anyone flying in late or leaving before dawn — a great many reviews across every platform say the same thing: "perfect for one night before your flight" · Beyond being near the airport, it's also close to Tiger Cave Temple, a major Krabi landmark, with retail shops and supermarkets like Tesco Lotus a short drive away · But the point to be clear about is that this location is not in the town center and not by the sea — it's about a 10–15 min drive into Krabi town and the night market, while Ao Nang Beach is about a 20–30 min drive away, and Railay is roughly 20 km plus a boat ride · The most common complaint in reviews is that there are limited dining options around the hotel — nearby you mostly have a 7-Eleven, and you'll need to drive to a mall or into town for a proper meal · The hotel offers airport transfers (for a fee) and can help arrange cars/tours · In short, Nap Krabi's location suits people who put "near the airport" first, or who have a car / don't mind calling a ride, more than those who want to step out of their accommodation and walk straight to the sea, a market, or restaurants

"Our flight landed late, so we booked here for one night before catching the boat to the islands the next morning · The room was clean, there was a pool to swim in, the staff were lovely, and it really is close to the airport like the reviews say · The only catch is that food is hard to find around the hotel — just a 7-Eleven, so you have to drive into town."

Room types and decor — Nap Krabi Hotel is a mid-size hotel with 80 rooms in total, and a detail many people like is that every room has a private balcony · Room types span several tiers, starting with the Superior, a standard room with a king or twin beds, moving up to the Deluxe, which is roomier and better appointed, a Triple for three people or a family, and a Suite for those who want more space · The decor is a simple, modern, light-toned style that leans on cleanliness and function rather than luxury flourishes, which fits its role as a stay-before-your-flight hotel · Every room has air conditioning, a flat-screen TV, a fridge/minibar, tea/coffee-making facilities, and free toiletries · What reviews agree on is that the rooms are clean, big enough, and look newer than you'd expect at this price, with the cleanliness score on Booking.com sitting high at around 7.8 and on TripAdvisor reaching as high as 4.8 out of 5 at times · Having a balcony in every room is something many people like for stepping out into the breeze, though it's worth noting that some balconies have no table or chairs to sit on, so you can stand and catch the air more than sit and sip coffee · A frequent observation in reviews is that soundproofing between rooms isn't great — you can hear the neighboring room or the hallway on some nights — and some rooms have issues with the hot water not getting hot enough or a damp bathroom, while the air conditioning in some rooms is slow to cool or hard to regulate · Another thing reviews flag is that on some platforms you may be assigned a lower floor, so if you care about the view or floor, ask for it when you book or check at check-in

Amenities, pool, and gym — what sets Nap Krabi apart from the usual near-airport accommodation is having an outdoor pool with a separate kids' pool and a gym with cardio and weight-training equipment · For a hotel with a low starting price aimed at short stays, having a pool to soak in and cool off after a day of travel, plus a gym for anyone who wants to work out, is an advantage many reviews mention — especially families with kids who get a kids' pool to play in · But to be honest, the pool isn't big — it's a compact pool for soaking and splashing rather than serious lap swimming, and there are reviews saying the pool is fairly small and gets crowded at times · Beyond the pool and gym there's also free private parking, a genuine advantage for self-drivers or those renting a car, a 24-hour front desk that helps with late check-ins for people arriving on evening flights, a bar/lounge for a casual drink, luggage storage, laundry/dry-cleaning, daily housekeeping, and a desk to help arrange tours, car rentals, and airport transfers (for a fee) · Wi-Fi is a particular high point — reviews on Booking.com rate the free Wi-Fi as high as around 10 out of 10, reflecting a stable, well-working connection · Overall the amenities here are "beyond expectations" for a near-airport hotel, because you get a pool, a gym, and free parking, which most places around the airport don't have

Food and nearby dining — on the food front at Nap Krabi, it has to be said honestly that it's not a main selling point and it's the most-criticized aspect · The hotel has a restaurant/bar that mainly serves breakfast (starting around 7 AM), and the breakfast earns praise from many reviewers as "good" and filling enough to start the day · But the point to understand is that the hotel restaurant has limited hours and closes fairly early (one review says it closes around 9 PM), and there's no room service after a set time · More importantly, there are almost no restaurants within walking distance of the hotel — a great many reviews stress that nearby you mostly have a 7-Eleven, and you'll need to drive to a mall or into town for a proper meal · So if you arrive late and hungry, plan ahead by picking up something to eat before reaching the hotel, or ask the front desk about places that deliver · One thing that helps offset this is that a roughly 10–15 min drive into Krabi town gets you to a night market and seafood restaurants that are cheap and tasty · In short, judging only by food in and around the hotel can feel frustrating, but with good planning — eat breakfast at the hotel, then head out for other meals in town or order delivery — the food side is manageable, and you shouldn't expect a near-airport hotel like this to have full dining like an in-town resort

Service — service is an area that earns consistent praise and a key reason the overall score holds up for Nap Krabi · Many reviews describe the staff as very friendly, smiling, and helpful beyond expectations — some even use the words "the staff are lovely and incredibly helpful" · The staff category on Booking.com sits high at around 8.1, above the hotel's overall score, reflecting that real guests are impressed with the welcome · The 24-hour front desk helps a lot for people arriving late on evening flights or leaving before dawn to catch a plane · But in fairness, there's a service issue worth watching that comes up in reviews too, specifically airport transfers that are sometimes mishandled — one review tells of booking a ride to the airport in advance and confirming it with the front desk, only for the driver not to show up on time, nearly missing the flight · This is something to be especially careful about, because the hotel's selling point is its proximity to the airport · The advice is, if you book a transfer, confirm it again the night before, and have a backup plan ready with a ride-hailing app or a taxi number · Overall, service still leans positive, but transfer coordination is a point you shouldn't rely on one hundred percent

What real reviews say (the good and the bad) — pulling together Booking.com (scoring around 7.1–7.8 from several hundred guests · with hundreds of reviews accumulated), TripAdvisor (around 3.7 out of 5 · ranked roughly #41 of 94 hotels in Mueang Krabi) and other booking platforms, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: genuinely close to Krabi Airport as reviews say, great for a stay before or after a flight; rooms clean, looking new, and big enough (high cleanliness score); friendly, helpful staff (staff score around 8.1); a pool and kids' pool, which are rare in near-airport accommodation; a gym and free parking; fast, stable Wi-Fi; good breakfast; and value for money that many describe as "paying this much and getting a pool, a gym, and being near the airport is a good deal" · On the watch-out side: the most-mentioned point is a location far from the sea, markets, and restaurants — around the hotel it's almost all 7-Eleven, and you have to drive to a mall or into town; next is soundproofing between rooms isn't great, hearing the neighboring room and the hallway on some nights; some bathrooms have hot water that isn't hot enough or feel damp; the air conditioning in some rooms is slow to cool or hard to regulate; the pool is fairly small and gets crowded at times; some room balconies have no table or chairs; the hotel restaurant closes early; and airport transfers that have been mishandled before · Almost all of these criticisms are things you can manage by setting expectations to match "a near-airport hotel with a pool," choosing your room and confirming your transfer carefully, rather than being big problems that keep people from coming back — reflected in an overall score that remains in satisfying territory

"The room was clean, the bed comfortable, and the staff actually arranged a car to the airport for us before dawn · Really close to the airport, true to the name · The only catch is the walls are thin and you hear the room next door a bit, and the hot water in the morning wasn't very hot — next time I'll ask to check the room first."

Price and value — Nap Krabi Hotel's starting price is about THB 600/night at regular rates (on some platforms and during promotions / low season it has dipped to around THB 500–600, or roughly 15–16 dollars), rising to around THB 1,200–1,800+ for a Deluxe, Triple, or Suite during high season or long weekends · Compared with near-airport accommodation of the same level in Krabi, Nap Krabi feels great value within the group of near-airport hotels that have a pool and a gym, because most similarly priced places around the airport don't have a pool or gym to use · Compared with staying at an Ao Nang-side resort from the very first night, this saves on the room rate and removes the problem of a long drive in the small hours after landing · But understand that what you "don't" get is a beachfront location, a bay view, restaurants all around, and the convenience of walking to the night market · A strategy many people use that pays off is to stay at Nap Krabi on the first or last night of the trip that's tied to a flight, then stay by the sea in the middle of the trip — you get both the airport convenience and the beach atmosphere without burning an expensive beachfront night just sleeping while you wait on a flight · Plan it this way and every baht you spend on Nap Krabi pays you back well in its role

What to know before you book — a few things help make the stay go smoother · One, be clear about the location — Nap Krabi stands out for being near the airport, not near the sea or a market; Ao Nang Beach is about a 20–30 min drive away and dining around the hotel is limited, so if you don't have a car, sort out ride-hailing or delivery in advance · Two, if you book an airport transfer, confirm it again the night before and have a backup plan, because some reviews have run into a no-show driver — keep a ride-hailing app or a taxi number ready so you don't miss your flight · Three, if you're a light sleeper sensitive to noise, ask for a room not next to the main hallway, because soundproofing between rooms isn't great · Four, check the bathroom for hot water and dampness at check-in, and if the water isn't hot or the room feels damp, tell the front desk to move you or fix it · Five, the hotel has a pool and a kids' pool, good for families, but the pool isn't big and gets crowded at times, so set expectations to a soak-and-cool-off pool rather than a lap pool · Six, plan for dinner — the hotel restaurant closes early and it's all 7-Eleven nearby, so if you arrive late and hungry, buy something to eat beforehand or ask about places that deliver · Seven, if you're self-driving, the free parking is an advantage · Eight, during high season (November–April) Krabi is busy and prices climb, so book ahead, compare prices across several platforms, and pick free cancellation up front if your plans aren't set

The verdict — from all the real reviews, Nap Krabi Hotel is the best fit for people who want a place near Krabi Airport for the first or last night of a trip while still wanting a pool, a gym, and a clean room · Being just a 5–10 min drive from the airport, with a pool and kids' pool, a gym, free parking, fast and stable Wi-Fi, friendly staff, and an accessible price, makes it good value that's hard to match among near-airport accommodation · But you have to accept honestly that this place is far from the sea, markets, and restaurants, with almost only a 7-Eleven nearby, soundproofing between rooms that isn't great, some rooms with hot-water and dampness issues, a fairly small pool, and a history of mishandled airport transfers · If you're after a beachfront resort, a sea view, or a location where you step out and walk straight to markets and restaurants, this isn't the answer — look at the Ao Nang side, Railay, the islands, or a hotel in the town center instead · But for a Krabi trip where you want a clean place near the airport with a pool and gym on a light budget, for sleeping ahead of a flight or to start and close a trip — Nap Krabi Hotel is a well-suited choice in its role, and it's the reason it keeps earning a satisfying score from hundreds of guests

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Nap Krabi Hotel, Krabi

faq.q: How far is Nap Krabi Hotel from Krabi Airport?
faq.a: The hotel is on Phetkasem Road in Krabi Noi sub-district, just about 3–6 km, or a 5–10 min drive, from Krabi Airport (KBV) · It's the hotel's main selling point, great for anyone flying in late or with an early-morning flight · There's a 24-hour front desk for late check-ins and airport transfers (for a fee)

faq.q: Does Nap Krabi Hotel have a pool and a gym?
faq.a: Yes — an outdoor pool with a kids' pool, and a gym with cardio and weight equipment, which is rare in accommodation near Krabi Airport · The pool isn't big — it's a pool for soaking, cooling off, and letting kids play rather than serious lap swimming, and reviews say it gets crowded at times · But at this price and with a near-airport location it's an advantage, and good for families

faq.q: What's the starting price at Nap Krabi Hotel · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 600/night at regular rates (during some promotions it has dipped below that, to around 15–16 dollars) · There are Superior, Deluxe, Deluxe Triple, and Suite rooms, and every room has a private balcony · Family rooms and suites can climb to around THB 1,200–1,800+ during high season (Nov–Apr), so compare several platforms before booking

faq.q: Who is Nap Krabi Hotel for?
faq.a: It's great for travelers with late-night or early-morning flights, anyone stopping for a night before or after a flight, small families who want a kids' pool, and self-drivers who want free parking · If you're after a beachfront resort, a sea view, or a location within walking distance of markets and restaurants, the Ao Nang side, Railay, the islands, or a hotel in the town center may suit you better

faq.q: Are there restaurants around Nap Krabi Hotel · what's the food like?
faq.a: The point to understand is that food is hard to find around the hotel — nearby it's almost all 7-Eleven, and the hotel restaurant mainly serves breakfast and closes fairly early · If you arrive late and hungry, buy something to eat beforehand or ask the front desk about delivery · A roughly 10–15 min drive into Krabi town gets you to a night market and seafood restaurants that are cheap and tasty · The hotel's own breakfast earns praise as good

faq.q: What's the noise and bathroom situation like at Nap Krabi Hotel?
faq.a: Many reviews agree that soundproofing between rooms isn't great, hearing the neighboring room and the hallway on some nights · And some reviews report hot water that isn't very hot or a damp bathroom, plus air conditioning in some rooms being slow to cool · If you're a light sleeper, we recommend asking for a room not next to the main hallway and checking the hot water and bathroom dampness at check-in, so you can ask to change rooms in time if you find a problem
